guide.summary: Holy sites, museums and gardens, with breakfast cafés, a bakery, dinners and a cocktail bistro checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Saturday is the main museum closing day: the Bible Lands Museum, Museum of Tolerance Jerusalem and Menachem Begin Heritage Center are closed on Saturday, and the Friends of Zion Museum is closed on Sunday as well.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.value: Saturday, plus Sunday at Friends of Zion
toolkit.copy: The Bible Lands Museum, Museum of Tolerance Jerusalem and Menachem Begin Heritage Center are closed on Saturday, and the Friends of Zion Museum is closed on Sundays, Saturdays and holidays. The Eucalyptus is closed on Friday and Saturday.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: The Western Wall Heritage Foundation says the Tunnels tour must be reserved in advance and can only be toured with a certified guide. The Bible Lands Museum refunds cancellations made up to 48 hours before your visit, and the Hebrew Music Museum asks you to reserve places in advance.

toolkit.label: Table reservations
toolkit.copy: Machneyuda and Talbiye take bookings through their online links and do not accept email reservations. The Eucalyptus says reservation is required, and the Notre Dame Center Rooftop Restaurant recommends reserving.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: The Jerusalem Botanical Gardens does not admit bicycles or scooters and allows only guide or service dogs. The Notre Dame Center's Rooftop Restaurant and Bistro are not kosher, and the Austrian Hospice roof terrace charges 5 NIS per person, free for in-house guests.

guide.dek: Reserve the Western Wall Tunnels and your dinner tables ahead, and plan museum days around Saturday closures.
intro: Start at the Western Wall, where the Western Wall Heritage Foundation says the Prayer Plaza is open all day, every day of the year. The Western Wall Tunnels work differently: the foundation says the tour must be reserved in advance and can only be toured with a certified guide, with entry Sunday to Thursday from 09:00 to 22:00 and on Friday from 09:00 to 13:00. Across the Kidron Valley, the Basilica of the Agony at the foot of the Mount of Olives opens 8:00 to 17:00 from October to March, and the Custody of the Holy Land asks visitors to show respect and keep silence.

Plan museum days around Saturday closures. The Bible Lands Museum on Shmuel Stefan Wise Street opens at 10:00 Sunday to Friday, stays open until 21:00 on Wednesday, closes at 14:00 on Friday and is closed on Saturday; a full-price ticket includes a free return visit within a month. The Museum of Tolerance Jerusalem on Hillel Street is also closed on Saturday and lists extra closures on 13, 19 and 22 November 2026. The Friends of Zion Museum runs tours Monday to Friday and is closed on Sundays, Saturdays and holidays.

With children, the Jerusalem Botanical Gardens on Yehuda Burla Street publishes separate summer and winter hours, is closed on Yom Kippur and does not admit bicycles or scooters; its Winter Dreams light exhibition runs from 17 November 2026 to 31 January 2027, starting at 17:00. The Bloomfield Science Museum sells tickets online, and the Hebrew Music Museum in Nahalat Shiv'a asks you to reserve places in advance. On Mount Zion, the Dormition Abbey church opens from 09:00 Monday to Saturday and from 11:30 on Sunday, and its cafeteria is closed on Sundays.

For food, Machneyuda on Beit Ya'akov Street opens 12:30 to 24:00, takes bookings online and does not accept email reservations. The Eucalyptus serves dinner Sunday to Thursday, is closed on Friday and Saturday and says reservation is required. The Notre Dame Center's Rooftop Restaurant opens Tuesday to Saturday evenings and recommends reserving, while its Bistro serves cocktails daily from 12:00 to 21:00. For mornings, Caffit on Emek Refaim opens at 07:30 Sunday to Wednesday, and Café Triest at the Austrian Hospice on the Via Dolorosa opens daily from 10:00.
summaryCards: Pair the Western Wall Prayer Plaza, open around the clock, with a pre-booked Western Wall Tunnels tour and the Bible Lands Museum, which is closed on Saturday.
Have breakfast at Caffit on Emek Refaim, which opens at 07:30 Sunday to Wednesday, then walk the Jerusalem Botanical Gardens, which open at 9:00.

Remember the Saturday closures at the Bible Lands Museum, Museum of Tolerance Jerusalem and Menachem Begin Heritage Center, the Sunday closure at the Friends of Zion Museum, and that The Eucalyptus requires a reservation and is closed on Friday and Saturday.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability, and many venues change hours around Shabbat and Jewish holidays. Several major sites could not be read by automated fetch and are left out: the Israel Museum (certificate error), Tower of David Museum, Yad Vashem, the Biblical Zoo and the Ramparts Walk (HTTP 403), and the Knesset (blocked by location). Some places were published only partially: the Western Wall has no street address (the Prayer Plaza is the location named); the Begin Heritage Center's hours appear reversed on its page; the Museum on the Seam's English and Hebrew hours conflict; Bloomfield Science Museum, Neeman Bakery branches, the King David Hotel and the Jerusalem Cinematheque publish no weekly hours on the pages read; Caffit (German Colony) omits Thursday and Hasadna omits Sunday and Monday. Gethsemane, the Austrian Hospice, Café Hillel, Friends of Zion Museum and the Hebrew Music Museum showed no 2026-dated content, so they rest on published hours notices.
